rationale: This completes Phase 4's delivery chain — the three pieces the owner ordered built today (2026-08-26, 'please go ahead with the remaining path') after ruling both open product questions: the review-item producer, the /d/ ZIP download link, and the delivery email's compose-and-send. Everything rides existing machinery where it exists: the PRODUCER is zero new Go (an agent seed driving the existing create_work_item action, whose own comment names status needs_human_review + no handler as the platform's HITL idiom, with spec_literal checkpoint:true satisfying the approve handler's second 400); /d/ is the pre-mint-and-refresh design the owner resolved on 2026-08-21 (DECISION_2026-08-21b): the presign is minted only by the spawned zip-deliverer (bugs_open/245 stands — no standing service touches object storage), stored on the token row (migration 650), and /d/ is pure DB->302; the EMAIL action composes from an OWNER-EDITABLE template in DB config (no roll to change copy; figures trace to the attested register) and sends through platform/mailer. THE ORDERING INSIDE THE SEND ACTION IS THE PART TO REVIEW HARDEST: the sender is constructed BEFORE delivery.Claim, and the template is validated against producible links BEFORE delivery.Claim, because Claim stamps the once-only handover — a failure discovered after the stamp strands the site handed-over-but-unemailed (recoverable only by the deliberate operator recipe in the seed header). Both pre-stamp guards are mutation-proved. The post-fill placeholder scan remains as the typo net, and its error says the stamp already happened rather than letting the operator find out at the next refused Claim. A DESIGN GAP FOUND MID-BUILD and closed before it shipped: {{zip_link}} with no presign supplied would have been REPLACED BY AN EMPTY STRING — a customer email reading 'Your files:' with nothing after it, invisible to the post-fill scan because the fill succeeded. The template-vs-links check refuses that shape pre-stamp. STALE /d/ LINKS: a stale stored presign is NEVER redirected to (an expired presign answers 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch, the LANDMINES trap that reads as broken credentials); the customer gets an honest 'being refreshed' page and the hit is PERSISTED to agent_error_log (code ZIP_LINK_STALE), the channel the fleet's triage sweeps — one stated deviation from DECISION_2026-08-21b §4's literal wording (a work item): the full work-item filing rides the refresher build, named openly rather than smuggled. The refresher itself (re-stamping stored_url before day 7) is the remaining unbuilt half and is stated as such everywhere.

edits.rationale: MintZipToken refuses an empty presign (a token that can only ever render the refresh page is a link born broken). LookupZipURL is ONE statement — purpose, expiry, revocation all in the WHERE so nothing changes between check and update; use_count increments on fresh AND stale (a stale visit is a use; it is what arms the refresh). ErrZipURLStale is deliberately distinct from ErrTokenNotFound: reaching it requires HOLDING a valid token, so distinguishing leaks nothing, and the customer-facing behaviour must differ — never redirect to a URL that will 403 as SignatureDoesNotMatch.
edits.sketch:
func LookupZipURL(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, plaintext string, now time.Time) (string, error) {
	var url sql.NullString
	var urlExpires sql.NullTime
	err := db.QueryRowContext(ctx, `
		UPDATE customer_access_tokens
		   SET use_count = use_count + 1,
		       used_at   = COALESCE(used_at, $3)
		 WHERE token_hash = $1
		   AND purpose    = $2
		   AND expires_at > $3
		   AND revoked_at IS NULL
		RETURNING stored_url, stored_url_expires_at
	`, HashToken(plaintext), PurposeZipDownload, now.UTC()).Scan(&url, &urlExpires)
	if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
		return "", ErrTokenNotFound
	}
	...
	if !url.Valid || url.String == "" || !urlExpires.Valid || !urlExpires.Time.After(now) {
		return "", ErrZipURLStale
	}
	return url.String, nil
}

edits.rationale: The bool became a hazard the day /d/ went real: it could mint a zip token with NO stored URL, which LookupZipURL correctly reads as stale — a link born broken that looks retriable. Claim now mints via MintZipToken only when a presign is supplied. ReviewItemKeyPrefix corrects the register-stated key shape to what the producer ACTUALLY files (create_work_item's convention: delivery_review_<domain>) — the register must state the real shape, not the shape a helper wished for.

GET-only (a download is idempotent; LookupZipURL mutates only use_count, which exists to measure exactly such visits — nothing a scanner can corrupt). 302 not 301: the target changes every refresh cycle. Stale renders the honest page AND records via deps (best-effort: failing to record must not break rendering); unknown gets the uniform failure page, same no-oracle rule as /c/. Registered in RegisterRoutes, the single route-table definition.

The /d/ test's expectation FLIPS from refused (yesterday: vouching for an unservable route) to accepted, with the admin-router refusal retained as the pairing that keeps the two lists' jobs distinct.

The chain's last step. ORDER IS THE DESIGN: (1) sender constructed BEFORE the claim — a missing SMTP secret fails with nothing stamped; (2) template validated against producible links BEFORE the claim — every optional link's availability is knowable from config, and {{zip_link}} with no presign would otherwise fill as an EMPTY STRING (a customer email reading 'Your files:' with nothing after it, invisible to any post-fill scan); (3) delivery.Claim = gate + once-only stamp + minting; (4) fill the CLOSED placeholder vocabulary and refuse survivors, with an error that says the stamp already happened and names the recovery recipe. ErrNotReviewed and ErrAlreadyDelivered surface verbatim: the first is the owner's gate working, the second is the double-send guard working. All three guards mutation-proved.

Standard registration beside create_work_item. Two optional input keys (zip_presigned_url, zip_presign_minutes) — far under the RFC_022 budget (N=10), and TestBudgetCronCountsLiteralMatchesTheRegistry passes with them counted.
